is_anopheles.evidence: The study uses Anopheles coluzzii, Anopheles gambiae, and Anopheles stephensi.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping of the kdr mutation in Anopheles coluzzii (Bama-R colony) in S1 Fig.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: S1 Fig (c) reports the kdr allele frequency (51.7%) and sample size (n=75) for the Bama-R colony.

african_field_population.evidence: The only genotyped mosquitoes are from the Bama-R laboratory colony (established from field-collected mosquitoes but maintained under selection pressure in the lab). The paper does not report genotype data for wild-caught field populations.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study testing the effect of atovaquone on parasite transmission in mosquitoes.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study mentions collection sites in Bama and Soumousso, Burkina Faso.

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study uses established laboratory colonies (Bama-R, G3, Anst-S) and standard experimental procedures.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data is provided in the main text and supplementary figures.

assessment.summary: This study investigates the efficacy of atovaquone (ATQ) in blocking Plasmodium falciparum transmission in insecticide-resistant Anopheles mosquitoes. While the paper includes genotyping of the kdr marker in a laboratory colony (Bama-R), it does not report genotype data for wild-caught field populations, rendering it ineligible under the criteria.
exclusion_reasons: The paper does not report genotype data for wild-caught field populations; the only genotyped mosquitoes are from a laboratory colony.
